definition: A technique for applying the visual or stylistic characteristics of one piece of content (such as an artistic style) to another piece of content while preserving its underlying structure or content.
details: Style transfer, originally popularized in the context of neural image style transfer, has since been extended to other modalities like text style transfer, changing tone or formality while preserving underlying meaning.

explainer.lead: Style transfer applies the visual or stylistic characteristics of one piece of content to another while preserving the underlying structure or content. It matters because it lets systems restyle content without rebuilding it.

tiers.eli5: It is like repainting a photo in the style of a famous painter while the scene stays the same.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use neural image style transfer and extend it to text, changing tone or formality while keeping meaning. A pitfall is that restyling can drift from the original content.
tiers.paperLevel: A technique for applying the stylistic characteristics of one content piece to another while preserving its underlying structure or content; originally popularised in neural image style transfer and extended to text style transfer.

explainer.example: A model renders a photograph in the brushwork of a given painting while the depicted scene remains recognisable.
